jobs.title: Chief Program Officer (CPO)
jobs.description:
Homeless Children’s Network

Position Title: Chief Program Officer (CPO)

SALARY: $190,000

SCHEDULE: Full-time position. Onsite/Hybrid ( In office 2-3 days per week)

BENEFITS: Health, Dental, and Vision insurance; Commuter stipend

HOMELESS CHILDREN’S NETWORK MISSION STATEMENT

Homeless Children’s Network’s (HCN) mission is to decrease the trauma of homelessness and domestic violence for children, youth, and families; to empower families; and to increase the effectiveness of collaborative efforts among service providers to end homelessness and poverty. Since 1992, HCN has empowered San Francisco’s underserved and historically marginalized communities citywide toward a brighter future with love, wholeness, and healing.

About Homeless Children’s Network (HCN)

Since 1992, HCN has been San Francisco’s leading nonprofit agency for comprehensive early intervention and mental health support for underserved and historically marginalized children, youth, and families experiencing homelessness, housing instability, or living in intergenerational poverty. Our mobile therapeutic model is both accessible and scalable, enabling clinicians to meet clients directly in the community. As the hub of a Collaborative of 60+ service agencies and community-based organizations, we serve over 2,500 clients each year, reaching those most reluctant to trust conventional mental health systems. Central to our work is our Afri-centric mental health and wellness model. This community-defined approach addresses health inequities and the persistent cycle of racism and trauma over generations. This model not only uplifts the Black/African American communities but also strengthens the behavioral health outcomes of all San Franciscans, fostering resilience, healing, and lasting change.

Position Summary

The Chief Program Officer (CPO) will be responsible for the overall management, strategic direction, and execution of all programs and services provided by Homeless Children's Network. This role requires a visionary leader with a strong background in program management, a deep understanding of our mission, and the ability to inspire and guide a diverse team. The CPO will work closely with the CEO and other executive leaders to ensure that our programs are effective, sustainable, and aligned with our strategic goals.

Duties And Responsibilities

Strategic Leadership Alignment

Provide end-to-end oversight of program goals/objectives and deliverables, ensuring 100% achievement of annual deliverables through ongoing monitoring, regulation, and performance management, and report directly to the CEO.
Deliver weekly data-driven reports to the CEO, providing clear visibility into program performance, progress, and outcomes.
Develop and implement the strategic direction for all programs, aligned with the organization’s mission and goals.
Collaborate with the executive team to shape the organization's long-term strategic vision.
Lead the development of new programs and services to meet emerging needs within the community.

Program Management Alignment

Proactively communicate high-priority information to the CEO through both verbal and written channels, ensuring timely awareness and decision-making.
Provide clinical programming and guidance to Clinical Supervisors and Program Directors, ensuring quality of care and adherence to best practices.
Oversee clinical program strategy and operations, ensuring effectiveness, compliance, and alignment with organizational goals.
Oversee the planning, implementation, and evaluation of all programs to ensure they are delivered efficiently and effectively.
Ensure compliance with all relevant regulations, policies, and ethical standards.
Monitor program budgets to ensure resources are allocated effectively and financial objectives are met.

Team Leadership Alignment

Maintain a collaborative reporting relationship with the COO, incorporating feedback to strengthen cross-functional alignment (approx. 15% focus).
Lead, mentor, and develop program managers and staff, fostering a culture of collaboration, innovation, and excellence.
Provide ongoing training and professional development opportunities for program staff.
Promote a positive and inclusive work environment that values diversity and teamwork.

Stakeholder EngagementAlignment

Build and maintain strong relationships with key stakeholders, including funders, community partners, and government agencies.
Represent the organization at external events, conferences, and in the media.
Work closely with the development team to identify and pursue funding opportunities.

Program Evaluation and Reporting Alignment

Develop and implement systems to measure program outcomes and impact.
Analyze data to assess program effectiveness and make data-driven decisions to improve results.
Prepare and present regular reports to the CEO, board of directors, and funders.

Resource Development Alignment

Collaborate with the development team on grant writing and fundraising efforts.
Ensure financial sustainability by managing program budgets and seeking opportunities for program expansion.
Innovate and develop new programs or services that align with the organization’s mission.

Compliance and Risk Management Alignment

Ensure that all programs adhere to legal and regulatory requirements.
Identify potential risks related to program activities and develop mitigation strategies.
Implement policies and procedures to ensure program integrity and safety.

Required Qualifications

Education: Master’s degree in Public Administration, Social Work, Business Administration, or a related field.
Experience: Minimum of 10 years of experience in program management, with at least 5 years in a senior leadership role
Leadership Skills: Proven ability to lead and manage diverse teams, develop strategic initiatives, and execute complex projects.
Analytical Skills: Strong ability to evaluate program effectiveness, interpret data, and make informed decisions.
Communication Skills: Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to engage and influence a wide range of stakeholders.
Problem-Solving Skills: Creative and strategic thinker with the ability to develop innovative solutions to complex challenges.
Cultural Competence: Demonstrated ability to work effectively with diverse populations and a commitment to equity and inclusion.
Licensed as a Marriage and Family Therapist, MFTI, LMFT, LCSW, Clinical Social Worker or Psychologist

KEY PERFORMANCE INDICATORS

Successful implementation and impact of programs.
Achievement of budget and financial targets.
Employee satisfaction and retention rates.
Strength and number of external partnerships and stakeholder engagements.
Innovation and successful expansion of programs.

HCN’s Community Culture

Of all the above important qualifications, bring the heartfelt quality of compassion, with exquisite cultural responsiveness as a primary guiding quality, not only of your professional life, but of what you hold dear.

Please bring a strong analysis of how race, ethnicity, culture, language, region, poverty, sexual and gender identity, age, education, opportunities, and resources generationally made available or not, and systemic oppressions impact a person’s mental health.

Please share stories from your own life about how you have been a mover and shaker in transforming these systems.

Please accept that HCN is a vibrant community that has a legacy that is of interest to you, and is also prompted to grow steadily, and with the respect of what has been done well central in the conversation.

jobs.title: Founding COO (Dirty Water Brand)
jobs.description:
Launched in May 2024 with an industry, on-premise focus in NYC, Dirty Water is what lighter beer wants to be. The perfect sessionable balance between a beer and a seltzer, we are category defining it as “beer-seltzer.” Lightest in taste. Lightest in macros. Endlessly crushable. The perfect answer for "what's the lightest thing you got?" while still going strong at 4.5%.

It's for the people that love drinking classic light beers but don't love the carbs and calories. It's for the people who love the macros of a hard seltzer but don't love the artificial fruity flavors or the variety packs. Pure leisurely drinking.

We just recently launched our second SKU which targets the single serving, grab-n-go format. A 24oz can called “Dirties Menthol.” It is a lemon-ice flavor with a mentholated cooling effect, 7% ABV. The packaging looks like a cigarette.

Dirty Water in nature has counter-culture roots while still able to hit the mass market.
@dirtywaterworld

The Real Talk

This role will require a lot of time and effort with possibility of very little in return. But there is also a possibility for this to be the most important work of your career with an incredibly high upside. Things that may feel remedial may be necessary. Nothing is beneath any of us. We're a young brand with a very focused vision and people who aren't afraid to get dirty, ruffle some feathers and stand shoulder to shoulder with the big macro brands.

The Role

We're looking for a Founding COO to build the operating engine of this company alongside the founder. Not an advisor. Not a consultant. We're looking for a partner who has done this before, knows where the bodies are buried in this industry, and wants to do it again with a brand worth betting on.

You have taken new beer brands from a single market to national relevance. You know what a distributor actually responds to. You've sat in the truck on ride-alongs, walked the back bar, argued about shelf sets, sweated a production run, and built the forecast that told everyone whether any of it was working. You've done the glamorous parts and the unglamorous parts, and you know the unglamorous parts are where brands are actually won.

You'll be responsible for growing national/key accounts while also working with the founder on operations, production, forecasting and whatever else is necessary. Then you'll go get in the market too, because that's the job at this stage.

Location:
Open. Preference for the Midwest or New England. NYC presence is not required, but regular travel to market is.

Compensation:
Salary plus meaningful equity.

Experience and Requirements

10+ years in the beer, seltzer or broader alcoholic beverage industry, with significant time inside emerging or challenger brands rather than only large established portfolios.
Proven experience building and managing national account relationships, including chain presentations, category reviews, and the annual cycles that come with them.
Deep distributor experience. You've built wholesaler relationships from the ground up, run crew drives and GSMs, done ride-alongs, and know how to earn mindshare from reps who have 200 other brands in the bag.
Both on-premise and off-premise sales experience, with a clear point of view on how the two feed each other.
Experience building trade and marketing strategy, including pricing and promo architecture, POS programs, and activation calendars that actually move volume.
Hands-on production experience. You've managed co-packing relationships, planned and attended production runs, and dealt with the reality of QA issues, supply timing, and inventory that arrives late.
Strong command of budgets, forecasting and unit economics. You can build a plan, defend it, and tell the difference between a bad month and a bad model.
Comfortable with early-stage ambiguity, thin resources, and doing the work yourself before there is anyone to delegate it to.
Willing to work non-traditional hours and travel regularly.

Key Responsibilities﻿National Accounts and Commercial Strategy

Build the national account roadmap - which chains, in what order, on what timeline, and what has to be true before we walk in the door.
Own chain presentations, category review cycles, and the follow-through that keeps placements alive after the win.
Develop pricing and margin architecture that works across markets and doesn't box us in as we scale.
Identify which markets we open next and build the case for each one.

Distributor Management

Own the wholesaler relationship end to end, starting with our NYC metro partners and extending into new markets as we expand.
Set goals, priorities and incentives with distributor leadership, then hold the line on execution.
Run crew drives, general sales meetings, ride-alongs and market work with rep teams.
Build the reporting and depletion tracking cadence that tells us the truth about what's happening in market.

Trade and Marketing Strategy

Build the annual trade calendar - programs, promotions, POS, incentives, activations.
Work with the sales team to translate brand strategy into things that happen at the account level.
Make sure our spend goes where it compounds, and kill the stuff that doesn't.

Production and Operations

Manage co-packing relationships, production scheduling and run oversight.
Own raw materials, packaging and inventory planning across SKUs.
Build the operational systems this company will need at 10x volume, and keep them simple enough to actually use today.
Solve the logistics problems that come with a growing footprint - freight, warehousing, keg programs, DTC fulfillment.

Finance and Planning

Own budgeting, forecasting and cash planning alongside the founder.
Build and maintain the operating model that connects production, inventory, depletions and cash.
Support fundraising with the numbers, the plan and the credibility that comes from having done this before.

Partnership

Be a real thought partner to the founder on strategy, hiring, and the hard calls.
Help build a culture that stays scrappy and honest as the team grows.
Represent Dirty Water anywhere it needs representing, from a distributor boardroom to a bar at 11pm on a Tuesday.

What We're Not Looking For

Someone who needs a fully built org to be effective. Someone who wants to run this from a distance. Someone whose best work is behind them.

How to Apply

Send a note with any relevant information along with your resume and let's find time to hop on a call.

About The Role

Corporate Banking is seeking a Managing Director who will serve as a senior leader of the Sovereign Advisory function within Public Sector Banking (PSB). The PSB serves the financial services needs of Citi's government and public sector clients across the NAM, LATAM, EMEA, and APAC regions. The MD position will be based in New York or London and will lead the Sovereign Advisory team globally, driving the delivery of client rating and debt advisory and advisory-linked solutions in close coordination with regional and product partners across all geographies.

Sovereign Advisory is fully integrated with the PSB client strategy and Citi's PSB Sovereign Advisory strategy at a global level. The Sovereign Advisory function is structured to work closely with every product group at Citi, allowing the MD to shape and influence diverse financial strategies and maintain a broad, firm-wide perspective.

Core Responsibilities

The scope of work is global, encompassing all regions in which PSB operates, and focuses on leading the assessment, monitoring, and management of structural, macroeconomic, financial, and high-frequency data to understand, analyze, and forecast economic policy and fiscal/debt sustainability trends worldwide. The MD will advise on and customize Citi solutions for PSB clients across sovereign, multilateral, and public sector segments.

The work of the MD will consist, on the advisory side, of leading a wide variety of complex projects requiring macroeconomic analysis, sovereign credit, and political risk assessment, as well as sovereign debt sustainability analysis. The MD will contribute to originating episodic transactions and will drive client relationship business through targeted sovereign advisory at the most senior levels.

Key Responsibilities Include:

Strategic Leadership: Lead the global Sovereign Advisory function, setting strategic direction in alignment with PSB and Citi's broader public sector strategy.
Client Coverage & Origination: Drive origination and contribute to the execution of high-value sovereign advisory mandates across all regions (NAM, LATAM, EMEA, APAC), acting as the primary senior point of contact for key government and public sector clients.
Macroeconomic & Sovereign Analysis: Oversee and direct the maintenance of an extensive collection of global economic and financial data series, ensuring timely and accurate intelligence to inform client presentations and strategic decisions.
Market Monitoring: Lead monitoring of developments in the global economy and financial markets, providing senior-level insights and recommendations across all regions.
Senior Banker Support & Mentorship: Guide and mentor junior and mid-level bankers in country analysis, stress testing, and sourcing of relevant data; act as a senior resource for country, coverage, and product bankers on RfPs and transaction-related work such as due diligence, data, and scenario analysis.
Rating Methodology Expertise: Deep understanding of Sovereign and MDB/Supranational rating methodologies, as well as of the linkages between sovereigns and state-owned entities (SOEs) that impact rating assessments, is expected at this level.
Business Management: Lead strategic revenue analysis and franchise reviews in partnership with the Global Head of PSB and senior leadership. Oversee preparation of materials for Citi's most senior executives to present and speak at global events and conferences on government financing and public sector topics, requiring seamless coordination across regions and time zones.
Cross-functional Collaboration: Partner with every product group at Citi globally to deliver integrated, bespoke solutions for sovereign and public sector clients.

Qualifications

Work Experience and Academic Qualifications:

Advanced degree (Master's or PhD) with a strong quantitative background and thorough understanding of Economics, International Relations, Finance, or Public Policy Studies.
Minimum 15-20 years of progressive professional experience in Banking, Fixed Income, Emerging Markets Debt (research, sell-side/buy-side), or Rating Agencies, with demonstrated leadership at a senior level.
Prior experience working for a multilateral agency or international financial institution (e.g., IMF, World Bank, BIS, Central Bank) is highly valued.
Proven track record of originating and executing sovereign advisory transactions and managing senior client relationships across multiple regions.
FINRA licenses (SIE, S79, S63, S24)

Skills and Competencies:

Deep expertise in global macroeconomic and policy challenges, geopolitics, and economic development across Emerging and Developed Markets, with a comprehensive understanding of the Public Sector Industry.
Demonstrated leadership in employing quantitative modeling and research skills to drive economic and market analysis at a global scale.
Fluency in English is required; proficiency in another major language is an advantage given the breadth of global coverage.
Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Office; experience with Haver, Bloomberg, and other financial data platforms is expected.
Exceptional strategic and project management capabilities with strong analytic and financial acumen; ability to manage complex, multi-stakeholder engagements across regions and time zones simultaneously.
Outstanding interpersonal and leadership skills, with the ability to inspire and lead teams, while also engaging and influencing a broad group of Citi professionals and senior external stakeholders.

jobs.description:
DIRECTOR OF DEVELOPMENT

JOB DESCRIPTION

THE OPPORTUNITY

Filling in the Blanks (FITB) is looking for a Director of Development
who’s ready to turn passion into impact. This is a rare chance to build and lead a growing fundraising program from the ground up—cultivating donors, forging corporate and foundation partnerships, and driving the kind of sustainable growth that lets FITB reach more kids who need us. If you’re entrepreneurial, relationship-driven, and energized by big goals, this is your seat at the table.

ABOUT FILLING IN THE BLANKS

No child should go hungry just because the school week ended. That simple, urgent idea is what led New Canaan community activists Shawnee Knight and Tina Kramer to found Filling in the Blanks (FITB) in 2013—a Norwalk-based nonprofit built to close the weekend nutrition gap that too many families face.

Through its Weekend Meal Bag program, Fresh Food on the Move Mobile Pantry, and school-based distribution sites, FITB meets families exactly where they are—removing the logistical and financial barriers standing between kids and consistent, healthy food. Since its inception, FITB has delivered more than six million meals
to children across the region. Today, the organization reaches more than 10,000 students every week across 200+ sites
—powered entirely by volunteers, corporate partners, and individual donors. It’s a community-driven force for lasting change, and proof of what’s possible when a community decides that no child should go hungry on its watch. Learn more at fillingintheblanks.org.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Fundraising Strategy & Donor Relations

·      Develop and execute FITB’s annual fundraising plan and donor activities.
·      Secure financial support from individuals, foundations, and corporations.
·      Create and execute a strategy for a large, sustained base of annual individual and corporate donors.
·      Develop and maintain ongoing relationships with donors.
·      Identify and steward prospective donors.
·      Communicate with donors and staff via email, phone, or social media.
·      Use prospect research tools and donor database to build donor relationships.
·      Provide Co-Founders with information on donors they need to engage with directly.

Foundation & Corporate Fundraising

·      Develop and track proposals and reports for all foundation and corporate fundraising.
·      Collaborate with the marketing team to create solicitation materials for fundraising.

Events, Data & Reporting

·      Plan and execute all aspects of at least two fundraising events per year.
·      Ensure accurate and up-to-date records of donors and funding received are maintained.
·      Create funding targets for the Board of Directors.
·      Evaluate FITB’s annual fundraising plan and donor activities.

QUALIFICATIONS

Our ideal candidate will bring a strong commitment to the mission with the following skills and characteristics:
·      Bachelor’s degree required; Master’s degree a plus
·      5+ years of experience in development/fundraising
·      Demonstrated excellence in organizational, managerial, and communication skills

jobs.description:
Company Description

Revive Energy is a Montana-based advanced recycling and clean technology company developing a scalable solution for two of the world’s most persistent environmental challenges: end-of-life tires and hard-to-recycle plastic waste.

Every year, enormous quantities of plastics and tires are landfilled, stockpiled, burned, dumped, or otherwise discarded. Much of this material cannot be effectively or economically recycled using conventional methods and can remain an environmental liability for generations.

Our proprietary High-Power Density Catalyzed (HPDC) pyrolysis technology is designed to transform difficult-to-recycle plastics, tires, and other hydrocarbon-based waste into useful products.

Our initial commercial focus is end-of-life tires. This allows us to address a significant waste problem while further proving, scaling, and de-risking our technology for broader use with difficult-to-recycle plastics. Our process is designed to produce recovered tire pyrolysis oil (rTPO), recovered carbon black (rCB), recovered steel, and syngas that can help power the process itself.

With pilot-scale validation complete, Revive is preparing to build our Mini Commercial Prototype (MCP), the next step toward commercialization. The MCP will provide the foundation for scaling to our first 50-ton-per-day commercial facility and, ultimately, additional facilities across North America and beyond.

Revive is supported by a founding team and technical leadership with deep experience across engineering, energy infrastructure, technology commercialization, institutional finance, private equity, global supply chains, and strategic advisory.

Our Mission

Revive Energy was founded to help leave the world cleaner than we found it.
We believe technology and entrepreneurship can provide scalable solutions to waste problems that have persisted for generations. Our mission is to build and deploy technology capable of cleaning up end-of-life tires and difficult-to-recycle plastics at a scale that makes a meaningful difference.

Role Description

Revive Energy is looking for a Chief Executive Officer (CEO) to work directly with our Board of Directors and founding team through the company’s next stage of growth.

We need a builder.

The CEO will be responsible for building the business around our technology: raising capital, structuring the company, developing strategic partnerships, securing long-term commercial agreements, navigating corporate and regulatory requirements, and assembling the organization required to scale.
A major priority will be capital formation. The CEO will lead fundraising and financing efforts across institutional investors, strategic investors, private equity, family offices, infrastructure capital, lenders, project finance partners, and other sources of capital.

The CEO will also lead Revive’s commercial strategy, including securing long-term feedstock agreements, negotiating offtake agreements for our recovered products, and developing partnerships across the plastics, tire, automotive, chemical, energy, manufacturing, recycling, and waste industries.
Working with the Board and our professional advisors, the CEO will help establish the corporate structure, governance, compliance, financial controls, risk management, and operating systems needed to grow responsibly.

The immediate objective is clear: successfully advance the MCP, position Revive for our first 50-ton-per-day commercial facility, and build the foundation for a much larger company.

Qualifications

• Proven experience building or scaling an early-stage company, venture, or business.
• Demonstrated ability to raise meaningful outside capital and work effectively with investors, lenders, and strategic partners.
• Strong understanding of corporate finance, capitalization, deal structuring, budgeting, and financial planning.
• Experience negotiating significant commercial agreements, including strategic partnerships, supply or feedstock agreements, offtake agreements, joint ventures, or similar transactions.
• Experience establishing the corporate infrastructure required to scale, including governance, compliance, financial controls, risk management, and organizational structure.
• Experience working with Boards of Directors, investors, attorneys, accountants, regulators, lenders, and senior corporate decision-makers.
• Ability to recruit and lead an exceptional team through commercialization and growth.
• Strong communication, negotiation, business development, and relationship-building skills.
• Entrepreneurial, hands-on, and comfortable operating in an environment where the playbook is still being written.
• Experience in clean technology, energy, industrial technology, infrastructure, manufacturing, recycling, plastics, chemicals, tires, or waste is beneficial but not required.
• Prior CEO experience is welcome but not required. We care more about what you have built, financed, and accomplished than the titles you have held.

Compensation & Opportunity

This position will initially be equity-only, with a transition to competitive executive compensation anticipated as financing is secured. Location is flexible.

For the right person, this is an opportunity for meaningful ownership at a pivotal stage in Revive’s development. The technology has been validated at pilot scale, an experienced team is in place, and we
are preparing to build the MCP before moving to our first 50-ton-per-day commercial facility.

We are looking for an accomplished executive who could take another traditional leadership position but wants something more meaningful.

Someone who has already proven they can build something successful and wants the next thing they build to do some good in the world.

jobs.description:
About KulshanCLT

Kulshan Community Land Trust expands access to permanently affordable homeownership in Whatcom County, creating lasting opportunities for stability, equity, and belonging.

For more than 25 years, KulshanCLT has helped individuals and families purchase homes they can afford while preserving those homes as permanently affordable for future generations. Today, we are entering one of the most exciting periods in our history. We are completing new communities, expanding our homeownership and stewardship programs, and advancing a pipeline that will create many more permanently affordable homes throughout Whatcom County.

We are looking for a thoughtful, relationship-centered fundraising leader who believes housing can change lives—and who is excited to help build the partnerships and resources needed to make that possible. 

About the Position

The Director of Development is a senior leader responsible for creating and implementing a comprehensive fundraising strategy that supports KulshanCLT’s mission, programs, and long-term sustainability.

Working closely with the Executive Director, Board of Trustees, staff, donors, foundations, businesses, and community partners, the Director will strengthen existing relationships while building new sources of philanthropic support. The position will lead major giving, annual fundraising, institutional giving, corporate partnerships, planned giving, donor stewardship, fundraising events, and development operations.

This is both a strategic and hands-on role. The successful candidate will be comfortable developing a multi-year fundraising strategy, meeting personally with donors, reviewing a grant proposal, coaching a board member, analyzing fundraising data, and occasionally helping with the practical details that make an event successful.

The Director of Development supervises the Communications Lead and serves as a member of KulshanCLT’s leadership team.

Key Responsibilities Fundraising Strategy and Leadership

Develop and implement annual and multi-year fundraising plans aligned with KulshanCLT’s strategic and financial goals. 
Establish fundraising goals, revenue projections, donor-pipeline targets, and measures of success; monitor results and adjust strategies as needed. 
Partner with the Executive Director and Finance team on fundraising budgets and revenue forecasts. 
Foster a culture of philanthropy across staff, Board, homeowners, volunteers, and partners. 
Stay current on fundraising trends and opportunities relevant to affordable housing and community development. 

Major Gifts and Individual Giving

Build and actively manage a portfolio of current and prospective major donors, including identification, cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship. 
Create meaningful donor engagement through meetings, project tours, events, and other opportunities to connect with KulshanCLT’s work. 
Partner closely with the Executive Director on major-donor strategy, meetings, solicitations, and follow-up. 
Strengthen donor retention and engagement across first-time, recurring, lapsed, mid-level, and major donors. 
Lead annual appeals and individual-giving campaigns and develop KulshanCLT’s planned and legacy giving program. 

Foundation, Corporate, and Institutional Giving

Develop and manage a coordinated strategy for foundation, corporate, and institutional support. 
Cultivate relationships with foundations, banks, credit unions, businesses, and other funding partners while identifying new opportunities. 
Manage the grant calendar and ensure high-quality, timely proposals and reports in collaboration with program, finance, project development, and homeownership staff. 
Develop meaningful business partnerships that support KulshanCLT’s mission. 
Help plan and execute capital and project-specific fundraising campaigns. 

Board and Executive Partnership

Serve as staff liaison to the Board’s fundraising/development committee and help trustees participate effectively in fundraising and relationship-building. 
Partner with the Executive Director to cultivate relationships with donors, funders, community leaders, and strategic partners. 
Provide clear fundraising reports and updates to the Executive Director, leadership team, and Board. 
Participate in organizational planning, budgeting, and leadership discussions. 

Communications and Storytelling

Supervise and support the Communications Lead, including work planning, coaching, and performance management. 
Partner on donor communications, fundraising campaigns, impact stories, annual reports, and other materials that inspire engagement and giving. 
Ensure communications and fundraising strategies reinforce KulshanCLT’s mission, values, voice, and brand. 
Help identify and share compelling, respectful stories about homeowners, donors, projects, and community impact. 
Serve as a spokesperson and ambassador for KulshanCLT when appropriate. 

Events and Community Engagement

Develop and oversee fundraising and donor-engagement events, including the spring fundraiser, annual meeting, project tours, and smaller donor gatherings. 
Evaluate events for both fundraising results and relationship-building value. 
Represent KulshanCLT at community events, meetings, and presentations. 
Build relationships with civic leaders, businesses, housing partners, professional associations, and other community stakeholders. 

Development Operations, Data, and Systems

Ensure Salesforce provides accurate, useful donor and relationship information. 
Maintain consistent systems for tracking donor contacts, gifts, prospects, proposals, acknowledgments, and stewardship. 
Use dashboards, donor segmentation, prospect research, and giving history to guide fundraising decisions. 
Ensure gifts are acknowledged promptly and donor information is handled accurately and confidentially. 
Maintain effective development procedures and recommend technology or system improvements when needed.

Who We’re Looking For

A strong candidate will bring:

5 years demonstrated success in nonprofit fundraising, including individual giving, major gifts, grants, donor stewardship, or corporate partnerships. 
Experience developing and implementing annual or multi-year fundraising plans. 
A record of building authentic relationships and personally asking donors for support. 
Strong writing, editing, public speaking, and interpersonal communication skills. 
Experience working collaboratively with an executive director, board members, staff, volunteers, and community partners. 
Experience managing staff, consultants, or complex projects. 
Ability to create structure, establish priorities, track commitments, and consistently meet deadlines. 
Experience using a donor database or CRM; Salesforce experience is preferred. 
Comfort interpreting fundraising data, budgets, forecasts, and performance measures. 
Sound judgment, discretion, curiosity, and a willingness to communicate directly. 
Commitment to equity and an understanding of how housing affordability, wealth-building, and access to homeownership affect different communities. 
Ability to represent KulshanCLT warmly and professionally with a wide variety of people. 
A sense of humor and the flexibility to work in a growing organization where not every day goes exactly according to plan.

A specific degree is not required. We value relevant professional and lived experience and encourage candidates to apply even when they do not meet every listed qualification.  

Work Environment

This is a full-time, exempt position based in Bellingham, Washington. KulshanCLT currently supports a hybrid work arrangement, with approximately half of the position’s time spent in the office and the remainder working remotely or in the community.  

The position requires regular meetings with donors and partners throughout Whatcom County. Some evening and weekend work is required for events, donor gatherings, and community activities. Occasional travel within Washington may also be required.

Compensation & Benefits

$81,000 to $95,000- Exempt , depending on experience
Flexible schedule and some remote work options
Paid sick leave (per WA State law)
Generous PTO and paid holidays
Regence Health Insurance and MetLife Dental at 90 days
IRA and 3% employer match
Opportunities for professional development
Work with a mission-driven, collaborative team creating lasting community impact

How to Apply

Please submit a resume and cover letter describing your interest in KulshanCLT and how your experience prepares you for this role to
info@kulshanclt.org by August 25th
with the subject line Development Director Application. 

Kulshan Community Land Trust is an equal opportunity employer. We strongly encourage applications from people who have been historically underrepresented in nonprofit leadership, philanthropy, housing, and community development.

HOMELESS CHILDREN’S NETWORK MISSION STATEMENT

Homeless Children’s Network’s (HCN) mission is to decrease the trauma of homelessness and domestic violence for children, youth, and families; to empower families; and to increase the effectiveness of collaborative efforts among service providers to end homelessness and poverty. Since 1992, HCN has empowered San Francisco’s underserved and historically marginalized communities citywide toward a brighter future with love, wholeness, and healing.

About Homeless Children’s Network (HCN)

Since 1992, HCN has been San Francisco’s leading nonprofit agency for comprehensive early intervention and mental health support for underserved and historically marginalized children, youth, and families experiencing homelessness, housing instability, or living in intergenerational poverty. Our mobile therapeutic model is both accessible and scalable, enabling clinicians to meet clients directly in the community. As the hub of a Collaborative of 60+ service agencies and community-based organizations, we serve over 2,500 clients each year, reaching those most reluctant to trust conventional mental health systems. Central to our work is our Afri-centric mental health and wellness model. This community-defined approach addresses health inequities and the persistent cycle of racism and trauma over generations. Company Description

Revive Energy is a Montana-based advanced recycling and clean technology company developing a scalable solution for two of the world’s most persistent environmental challenges: end-of-life tires and hard-to-recycle plastic waste.

Every year, enormous quantities of plastics and tires are landfilled, stockpiled, burned, dumped, or otherwise discarded. Much of this material cannot be effectively or economically recycled using conventional methods and can remain an environmental liability for generations.

Our proprietary High-Power Density Catalyzed (HPDC) pyrolysis technology is designed to transform difficult-to-recycle plastics, tires, and other hydrocarbon-based waste into useful products.

Our initial commercial focus is end-of-life tires. This allows us to address a significant waste problem while further proving, scaling, and de-risking our technology for broader use with difficult-to-recycle plastics. Our process is designed to produce recovered tire pyrolysis oil (rTPO), recovered carbon black (rCB), recovered steel, and syngas that can help power the process itself.

With pilot-scale validation complete, Revive is preparing to build our Mini Commercial Prototype (MCP), the next step toward commercialization. The MCP will provide the foundation for scaling to our first 50-ton-per-day commercial facility and, ultimately, additional facilities across North America and beyond.

Revive is supported by a founding team and technical leadership with deep experience across engineering, energy infrastructure, technology commercialization, institutional finance, private equity, global supply chains, and strategic advisory.

Our Mission

Revive Energy was founded to help leave the world cleaner than we found it.
We believe technology and entrepreneurship can provide scalable solutions to waste problems that have persisted for generations. Our mission is to build and deploy technology capable of cleaning up end-of-life tires and difficult-to-recycle plastics at a scale that makes a meaningful difference.

Role Description

Revive Energy is looking for a Chief Executive Officer (CEO) to work directly with our Board of Directors and founding team through the company’s next stage of growth.

We need a builder.

new_jobs.title: Director of Development
new_jobs.description:
About KulshanCLT

Kulshan Community Land Trust expands access to permanently affordable homeownership in Whatcom County, creating lasting opportunities for stability, equity, and belonging.

For more than 25 years, KulshanCLT has helped individuals and families purchase homes they can afford while preserving those homes as permanently affordable for future generations. Today, we are entering one of the most exciting periods in our history. We are completing new communities, expanding our homeownership and stewardship programs, and advancing a pipeline that will create many more permanently affordable homes throughout Whatcom County.

We are looking for a thoughtful, relationship-centered fundraising leader who believes housing can change lives—and who is excited to help build the partnerships and resources needed to make that possible. 

About the Position

The Director of Development is a senior leader responsible for creating and implementing a comprehensive fundraising strategy that supports KulshanCLT’s mission, programs, and long-term sustainability.

Working closely with the Executive Director, Board of Trustees, staff, donors, foundations, businesses, and community partners, the Director will strengthen existing relationships while building new sources of philanthropic support. The position will lead major giving, annual fundraising, institutional giving, corporate partnerships, planned giving, donor stewardship, fundraising events, and development operations.

This is both a strategic and hands-on role. The successful candidate will be comfortable developing a multi-year fundraising strategy, meeting personally with donors, reviewing a grant proposal, coaching a board member, analyzing fundraising data, and occasionally helping with the practical details that make an event successful.

The Director of Development supervises the Communications Lead and serves as a member of KulshanCLT’s leadership team.

Key Responsibilities Fundraising Strategy and Leadership

Develop and implement annual and multi-year fundraising plans aligned with KulshanCLT’s strategic and financial goals. 
Establish fundraising goals, revenue projections, donor-pipeline targets, and measures of success; monitor results and adjust strategies as needed. 
Partner with the Executive Director and Finance team on fundraising budgets and revenue forecasts. 
Foster a culture of philanthropy across staff, Board, homeowners, volunteers, and partners. 
Stay current on fundraising trends and opportunities relevant to affordable housing and community development. 

Major Gifts and Individual Giving

Build and actively manage a portfolio of current and prospective major donors, including identification, cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship. 
Create meaningful donor engagement through meetings, project tours, events, and other opportunities to connect with KulshanCLT’s work. 
Partner closely with the Executive Director on major-donor strategy, meetings, solicitations, and follow-up. 
Strengthen donor retention and engagement across first-time, recurring, lapsed, mid-level, and major donors. 
Lead annual appeals and individual-giving campaigns and develop KulshanCLT’s planned and legacy giving program. 

Foundation, Corporate, and Institutional Giving

Develop and manage a coordinated strategy for foundation, corporate, and institutional support. 
Cultivate relationships with foundations, banks, credit unions, businesses, and other funding partners while identifying new opportunities. 
Manage the grant calendar and ensure high-quality, timely proposals and reports in collaboration with program, finance, project development, and homeownership staff. 
Develop meaningful business partnerships that support KulshanCLT’s mission. 
Help plan and execute capital and project-specific fundraising campaigns. 

Board and Executive Partnership

Serve as staff liaison to the Board’s fundraising/development committee and help trustees participate effectively in fundraising and relationship-building. 
Partner with the Executive Director to cultivate relationships with donors, funders, community leaders, and strategic partners. 
Provide clear fundraising reports and updates to the Executive Director, leadership team, and Board. 
Participate in organizational planning, budgeting, and leadership discussions. 

Communications and Storytelling

Supervise and support the Communications Lead, including work planning, coaching, and performance management. 
Partner on donor communications, fundraising campaigns, impact stories, annual reports, and other materials that inspire engagement and giving. 
Ensure communications and fundraising strategies reinforce KulshanCLT’s mission, values, voice, and brand. 
Help identify and share compelling, respectful stories about homeowners, donors, projects, and community impact. 
Serve as a spokesperson and ambassador for KulshanCLT when appropriate. 

Events and Community Engagement

Develop and oversee fundraising and donor-engagement events, including the spring fundraiser, annual meeting, project tours, and smaller donor gatherings. 
Evaluate events for both fundraising results and relationship-building value. 
Represent KulshanCLT at community events, meetings, and presentations. 
Build relationships with civic leaders, businesses, housing partners, professional associations, and other community stakeholders. 

Development Operations, Data, and Systems

Ensure Salesforce provides accurate, useful donor and relationship information. 
Maintain consistent systems for tracking donor contacts, gifts, prospects, proposals, acknowledgments, and stewardship. 
Use dashboards, donor segmentation, prospect research, and giving history to guide fundraising decisions. 
Ensure gifts are acknowledged promptly and donor information is handled accurately and confidentially. 
Maintain effective development procedures and recommend technology or system improvements when needed.

Who We’re Looking For

A strong candidate will bring:

5 years demonstrated success in nonprofit fundraising, including individual giving, major gifts, grants, donor stewardship, or corporate partnerships. 
Experience developing and implementing annual or multi-year fundraising plans. 
A record of building authentic relationships and personally asking donors for support. 
Strong writing, editing, public speaking, and interpersonal communication skills. 
Experience working collaboratively with an executive director, board members, staff, volunteers, and community partners. 
Experience managing staff, consultants, or complex projects. 
Ability to create structure, establish priorities, track commitments, and consistently meet deadlines. 
Experience using a donor database or CRM; Salesforce experience is preferred. 
Comfort interpreting fundraising data, budgets, forecasts, and performance measures. 
Sound judgment, discretion, curiosity, and a willingness to communicate directly. 
Commitment to equity and an understanding of how housing affordability, wealth-building, and access to homeownership affect different communities. 
Ability to represent KulshanCLT warmly and professionally with a wide variety of people. 
A sense of humor and the flexibility to work in a growing organization where not every day goes exactly according to plan.

A specific degree is not required. We value relevant professional and lived experience and encourage candidates to apply even when they do not meet every listed qualification.  

Work Environment

This is a full-time, exempt position based in Bellingham, Washington. KulshanCLT currently supports a hybrid work arrangement, with approximately half of the position’s time spent in the office and the remainder working remotely or in the community.  

The position requires regular meetings with donors and partners throughout Whatcom County. Some evening and weekend work is required for events, donor gatherings, and community activities. Occasional travel within Washington may also be required.

Compensation & Benefits

$81,000 to $95,000- Exempt , depending on experience
Flexible schedule and some remote work options
Paid sick leave (per WA State law)
Generous PTO and paid holidays
Regence Health Insurance and MetLife Dental at 90 days
IRA and 3% employer match
Opportunities for professional development
Work with a mission-driven, collaborative team creating lasting community impact

How to Apply

Please submit a resume and cover letter describing your interest in KulshanCLT and how your experience prepares you for this role to
info@kulshanclt.org by August 25th
with the subject line Development Director Application. 

Kulshan Community Land Trust is an equal opportunity employer. We strongly encourage applications from people who have been historically underrepresented in nonprofit leadership, philanthropy, housing, and community development.
